images.title: Halving 16 again and again
images.purpose: Shows a line of 16 units halved to 8, 4 and 2, with each length written as a power of 2.
images.composition: Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no people, no extra text. Four horizontal bars stacked one under another, all starting from the same left edge, each half as long as the one above.
images.exact_structure: Four horizontal bars, left ends aligned on one vertical line. Bar 1: 16 equal unit segments, teal (#0072B2). Bar 2: 8 unit segments. Bar 3: 4 unit segments. Bar 4: 2 unit segments. All unit segments are the same width. Bars 2 to 4 are teal (#0072B2) too, and the erased half of each is shown as a light grey (#6B7280) dashed outline to its right. To the right of each bar, in order: '2⁴ = 16', '2³ = 8', '2² = 4', '2¹ = 2'. On the left margin, 3 small amber (#E69F00) curved arrows from each bar to the next, each labelled '÷ 2'. Exactly 4 bars, 30 unit segments, 3 dashed outlines, 3 arrows.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec

images.takeaway: Each halving divides by 2 and takes one factor of 2 away from the exponent.
images.description: Shows a line of 16 units halved to 8, 4 and 2, with each length written as a power of 2.
images.teaching_notes: '÷ 2' appears 3 times. Ask how many halvings reach 1 unit.

image_decisions.why: Halving the 16-unit line is how the chapter introduces dividing powers; the bars show each factor of 2 disappearing.
